deep.reconstruction:
Context: the previous pages build functions u, v, w, ... that are continuous everywhere in an n-dimensional space except on cut surfaces, where they are left undefined. They are single-valued and continuous in the cut space. The bottom of the previous page also gives a group-theoretic argument: if a power A^N of a substitution is the identity, one descends through divisors to show A itself is the identity.

This page, step by step:

(1) Claim. Single-valuedness and continuity can hold together for such functions if and only if the (cut) space is simply connected. In modern terms: let X be a connected, locally path-connected domain. Every continuous 'multivalued function' obtained by continuation along paths (equivalently, every covering of X, or every locally constant system of branches) has a global single-valued continuous branch iff pi_1(X) = 1. This is the monodromy theorem together with its converse.

(2) Definition. 'Simply connected' may be defined outright by this property: every continuous function (in the continuation sense) is necessarily single-valued. This is a function-theoretic, Riemann-style definition, in place of the curve-contraction or cross-cut definitions.

(3) Programme. Transfer Riemann's theory of the multi-sheeted 2-dimensional surfaces belonging to an algebraic function of one variable to n dimensions. Take an n-dimensional space and give in it a branching locus B ('Verzweigungsgebilde'). On B the functions to be considered are declared undefined.

(4) Dimension claim: dim B = n-2. Modern justification (mine): a subset of codimension >= 3 does not change pi_1 of the complement locally, so it produces no monodromy. A codimension-1 set separates the space locally rather than being encircled by small loops. So only codimension 2 admits small linking circles around which branches can permute; this is the analogue of branch points in the plane.

(5) Cuts. One then lays cut-loci S ('Schnittgebilde'). Because they must separate the space, they must have dimension n-1. Their boundary is to lie solely in B; these are Seifert-surface-like hypersurfaces spanning B.

The next page continues: the cuts may meet along (n-2)-dimensional sets. They are to be chosen so that the cut space becomes simply connected; then u, v, w can be built there. B may have several irreducible components, each carrying an integer period nu (the order of the local monodromy around a small circle linking it; the simplest case is all nu = 2). The question then is the number of sheets of the covering, i.e. how many-valued the function is, given B and the periods.

Overall: this is a sketch of the theory of branched coverings of n-space (n-manifolds) branched along codimension-2 loci, set up by analogy with Riemann surfaces.
errors: The claim that cuts of dimension n-1, bounded only by the branch locus, can always be chosen so that the cut space becomes simply connected is unjustified in general. Example: R^3 minus a Seifert surface of a nontrivial knot has free, nontrivial fundamental group of rank 2g. What the construction actually needs is weaker: the monodromy of the intended covering must become trivial on the cut space. Full simple connectivity is more than needed and is not always achievable with such cuts. Additional cuts, as in Riemann's cross-cuts, may be required.

'Every continuous function is single-valued' as a definition of simple connectivity is only correct if 'continuous function' means a multivalued function defined by continuation (a covering or locally constant sheaf of branches). It also needs the space to be connected and locally path-connected. Taken literally for ordinary functions the statement is vacuous. The idea is right but loosely stated.

Dimension statements (n-2 for the branch locus, n-1 for the cuts) are asserted without proof. The n-2 claim is correct in substance, for real dimension and a tame locus. 'Necessarily' n-1 for the cuts is also correct in the sense of separating sets. Both are heuristic here.

results.what: Simple connectivity characterized or defined by: every continuous multivalued function (obtained by continuation) on the space is single-valued; this is necessary and sufficient for single-valued continuous branches.
results.modern_name: Monodromy theorem and its converse (pi_1 = 1 iff every covering of a connected, locally path-connected space is trivial)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (1851/1857, function-theoretic connectivity); Weierstrass; made precise via pi_1 by Poincaré (1895) and later covering-space theory (Weyl 1913, etc.)

results.what: Programme to generalize Riemann's multi-sheeted surfaces to n dimensions: a branched covering of n-space with branch locus of dimension n-2, cut along (n-1)-dimensional hypersurfaces bounded by the branch locus, with an integer period (local monodromy order) attached to each irreducible component.
results.modern_name: Branched coverings of n-manifolds along codimension-2 loci; cyclic branching indices; Seifert-type cut surfaces
results.usually_credited_to: Heegaard (1898), Wirtinger (1905, coverings of S^3 branched over knots), Tietze (1908), Alexander (1920); related ideas in Picard and Poincaré for algebraic surfaces (1880s-90s)

results.what: Branch locus must be of codimension 2.
results.modern_name: Codimension-2 nature of branch loci (purity of branch locus in algebraic settings: Zariski–Nagata)
results.usually_credited_to: Folklore from Riemann/Poincaré; algebraic purity by Zariski (1958) and Nagata

deep.surprise_reason: An early, explicit sketch of branched coverings of n-dimensional space is notable: codimension-2 branch locus, codimension-1 cuts bounded by it, cyclic periods per irreducible component, and the question of sheet number. It predates or parallels Heegaard and Wirtinger, depending on the notebook's date. But it is only a programmatic analogy with Riemann surfaces, and similar ideas were in the air via Riemann, Klein, Picard and Poincaré. No theorem is proved, and the simple-connectivity claim about the cuts is overoptimistic.

checkable.asserts: Local monodromy of z**(1/nu) around the branch locus has order nu (period nu): the branch reproduces after exactly nu circuits.
The function does not reproduce before nu circuits (the 'und nicht früher' condition) for nu=5.
Cuts of dimension n-1 have boundary of dimension n-2, matching the dimension of the branch locus they are bounded by.
The branch locus has real codimension 2, so small circles (1-spheres) link it, as for branch points in the plane (n=2).
